content: 1. Patients should be informed about substances they must avoid while taking Ezetimibe/Simvastatin and should promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness. They should also notify other physicians prescribing new medications that they are currently taking Ezetimibe/Simvastatin. 2. Cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis have been reported with ezetimibe, regardless of causality. Most patients who developed rhabdomyolysis were already on a statin before starting ezetimibe. However, rhabdomyolysis has been very rarely reported with ezetimibe monotherapy or when ezetimibe is added to agents like fibrates, which are associated with an increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. 3. Ezetimibe/Simvastatin is not recommended for patients with moderate or severe hepatic insufficiency due to unknown effects from increased exposure to ezetimibe in these individuals. 4. Potent inhibitors of CYP3A4, such as itraconazole, ketoconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone, and large quantities of grapefruit juice, increase the risk of myopathy by reducing the elimination of the simvastatin component of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin. 5. The risk of myopathy is increased by gemfibrozil and, to a lesser extent, by other fibrates and niacin (≥1 g/day). Concomitant administration of amiodarone or verapamil with higher doses of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin also increases the risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. 6. Cholestyramine reduces the mean AUC of total ezetimibe by approximately 55%, potentially diminishing the incremental LDL-C reduction achieved by adding ezetimibe to cholestyramine. 7. Concomitant administration of cyclosporine or danazol with Ezetimibe/Simvastatin increases the risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, particularly at higher doses. Cyclosporine concentrations should be monitored in patients receiving both medications, as increased exposure to both ezetimibe and cyclosporine may occur. 8. Fibrates may increase cholesterol excretion into bile, potentially leading to gallstone formation. Co-administration of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin with fibrates is not recommended until further studies are conducted. 9. Patients taking coumarin anticoagulants should have their prothrombin time monitored before starting Ezetimibe/Simvastatin and during early therapy to ensure no significant alterations occur. Once stable, monitoring can follow usual intervals. If the dose of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin is changed or discontinued, the same procedure should be repeated. 10. Simvastatin therapy has not been associated with bleeding or changes in prothrombin time in patients not taking anticoagulants. Ezetimibe (10 mg daily) had no significant effect on warfarin bioavailability or prothrombin time in healthy adults. 11. Optic nerve degeneration was observed in dogs treated with simvastatin at doses producing plasma drug levels approximately 12 times higher than those in humans taking 80 mg/day. Similar findings were noted with a chemically related drug in this class. 12. CNS vascular lesions, including perivascular hemorrhage, edema, mononuclear cell infiltration, fibrin deposits, and necrosis of small vessels, were observed in dogs treated with simvastatin at doses producing plasma drug levels about 14 times higher than those in humans taking 80 mg/day. 13. No evidence of mutagenicity or genotoxicity was observed in various in vitro and in vivo studies with the combination of ezetimibe and simvastatin or with ezetimibe alone. 14. In animal studies, ezetimibe was not carcinogenic, mutagenic, or toxic to reproduction at doses significantly higher than human exposure levels. However, increased incidences of common fetal skeletal findings were observed at high doses in rats and rabbits. 15. Simvastatin was not teratogenic in rats or rabbits at doses resulting in plasma drug levels three times higher than human exposure. However, skeletal malformations were observed in studies with a structurally related HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. 16. Vytorin (Ezetimibe/Simvastatin) is contraindicated in pregnancy (Category X). Treatment should be discontinued immediately if pregnancy is recognized. It should only be administered to women of childbearing potential if they are highly unlikely to conceive and have been informed of the potential risks. 17. The effects of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin on labor and delivery in pregnant women are unknown. 18. Women who are nursing should not take Vytorin due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants. It is unknown whether ezetimibe or simvastatin is excreted into human breast milk. 19. The safety and effectiveness of Vytorin in pediatric patients have not been established. Limited data exist for ezetimibe in adolescents with homozygous sitosterolemia or homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Treatment in children under 10 years is not recommended. 20. Simvastatin has been evaluated in adolescents (10–17 years) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Doses greater than 40 mg have not been studied in this population. Adolescent females should be counseled on appropriate contraceptive methods while on therapy. 21. In clinical studies, the safety of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin in patients aged 65 and older was similar to that in younger patients. However, greater sensitivity in some older individuals cannot be ruled out.
